Cigna Appeals Unit

Date: [Date of submission]

Re: Formal appeal of prior authorization denial  
Member: Riley Lawson  
Member ID: W461122627  
Reference number: POC-5D67837DC3-99680  
Requested service: ACL reconstruction  
CPT: 29888  
Denial date: August 18, 2026

Dear Cigna Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for medically necessary ACL reconstruction. The denial states that the submitted documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I request reversal of the denial and authorization for CPT 29888.

The medical record establishes the following:

- I have had 18 months of progressive knee pain that has not resolved with rest.
- I completed 16 weeks and 16 visits of supervised physical therapy from March 13, 2026, through July 3, 2026. Treatment included range-of-motion work and quadriceps strengthening. The physical therapy discharge note documents completion of this course.
- I used NSAIDs for eight months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 28, 2026, provided only four weeks of partial relief.
- MRI on June 28, 2026, demonstrated a complete mid-substance ACL tear with a bone-bruise pattern. The menisci were intact, and there was no significant arthritis.
- I have recurrent instability with pivoting and have experienced two episodes of giving way on stairs.
- Examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- There is no active infection or untreated substance use. My BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker.

These records address the duration and severity of symptoms, failure of substantial conservative treatment, objective MRI confirmation of a complete ACL tear, recurrent functional instability, and examination findings. They also provide relevant information regarding conditions that could otherwise affect surgical review.

The publicly available Cigna/EviCore guideline identified as CMM-312, Knee Surgery—Arthroscopic and Open Procedures, effective March 7, 2026, includes an ACL Reconstruction and Repair section. The guideline states that coverage determinations consider the applicable benefit plan, laws and regulations, relevant coverage policies, and the specific facts of the case. Cigna Medical Coverage Policy 0515 also states that ACL-related ligament allograft materials may be medically necessary when medical necessity has been established for the associated primary knee procedure.

I have not quoted the detailed ACL medical-necessity criteria because the complete text of the ACL subsection was not available in the policy text retrieved for this appeal. Please identify the exact criteria applied to this request and the specific documentation that Cigna considers missing. If additional information is required, please allow submission of that information and reconsider the request based on the enclosed records.

Please review the attached documentation:

1. June 28, 2026 MRI report;
2. Physical therapy discharge note documenting 16 completed visits from March 13 through July 3, 2026;
3. Medication and treatment history documenting eight months of NSAID use and the May 28, 2026 corticosteroid injection;
4. Orthopedic examination and clinical evaluation by Lindqvist, MD;
5. Operative recommendation and prior authorization materials for CPT 29888.

Because the denial was based on incomplete documentation rather than a finding that the surgery is not medically necessary, I request prompt reconsideration and approval of ACL reconstruction. Please provide the appeal decision in writing and include the clinical rationale and any criteria relied upon.

Sincerely,

Riley Lawson
